# INC-2026-041 post-mortem (Relay backpressure, 2026-04-14)
**Severity:** SEV-2 **Duration:** 47 minutes (14:12 to 14:59 UTC) **Affected services:** Crossguard NATS relay, both federated clusters (Low/High) **Customer impact:** ~4% of posts on federated channels delayed by up to 12 minutes, no data loss confirmed.
## Summary
At 14:12 UTC the NATS-side relay workers on `high.test` began accumulating unacked messages after a spike in post volume on ~engineering-updates. The outbox table grew to ~58k rows before the queue drained. Root cause was a missing backpressure signal between the publisher loop and the NATS writer; an earlier retry change made retry attempts effectively unbounded.
## Timeline (UTC)
| Time | Event | |-------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------| | 14:10 | Volume on ~engineering-updates spikes 6x baseline (release thread) | | 14:12 | First alert: `relay_outbox_unacked > 5000` fires on `high.test` | | 14:14 | On-call acks page, confirms workers are alive but not draining | | 14:18 | Failed mitigation: worker pool restart; outbox keeps growing | | 14:24 | Second alert: `relay_worker_retry_rate` saturates at configured cap | | 14:31 | Mitigation: flipped `CROSSGUARD_MAX_INFLIGHT` from unset to 256 | | 14:36 | Outbox starts draining, ~400 msg/s sustained | | 14:59 | Queue returns to 0, alerts clear, service declared healthy | | 15:30 | Comms posted to ~ops-announce and federated partners |
## Root cause
Commit `8f2a9c1` (2026-04-08) replaced the fixed-size retry pool with an unbounded goroutine-per-message fan-out. Under spike load this caused:
1. The NATS writer's internal buffer to fill, blocking the next `Publish`. 2. Retries queued faster than they drained, burning CPU on reschedules. 3. No upper bound on inflight publishes, so memory grew linearly with the outbox.
The dashboard showed the symptoms but did not distinguish between "writer slow" and "too many retries in flight," which delayed the correct mitigation by about 15 minutes.
## What went well
- Alerting fired within 2 minutes of the SLO breach - No data loss: all ~58k messages eventually acked - Azurite-backed dev env let us reproduce within 30 minutes post-incident
## What went poorly
- The unbounded-fanout change had a design review but no load test - Runbook didn't mention `CROSSGUARD_MAX_INFLIGHT` as a mitigation lever - No automated throttle, manual knob only
## Action items
- [ ] [CG-431] Cap inflight publishes per worker (hard), owner: @alice, by 2026-04-28 - [ ] [CG-432] Add `relay_writer_blocked_seconds` metric and alert, owner: @bob, by 2026-04-28 - [ ] [CG-433] Runbook: document the mitigation knob with example values, owner: @carol, by 2026-04-22 - [ ] [CG-434] Load test gate in CI for any change touching `server/relay/`, owner: @dave, by 2026-05-05 - [ ] [CG-435] Review all unbounded goroutine-per-item patterns in the codebase, owner: @alice, by 2026-05-12
Representative log line captured on `high.test` at 14:17 UTC:
``` level=error error_code=13421 msg="invalid payload" text="<Message> exceeded 65535 chars" peer=high.test team=cross-guard-team & channel=engineering-updates ```
